SETUP. 17 evidence questions vs 3 absence questions. bm25() in FTS5 is negative and ORDER BY ASC ranks best first, so MORE NEGATIVE IS A BETTER MATCH. Two query shapes, because the front door and the earlier probe do not agree: AND is what corpus_search.py actually builds, since fts_quote() emits quoted terms and FTS5's implicit operator is AND; OR is diagnose_recall.py's finding-B proxy, capped at 12 tokens. Neither is the agent's real query - the agent invents short phrases - so the two bracket its behaviour rather than reproducing it.

RESULT 1, AND IS THE FRONT DOOR'S OWN FAILURE MODE. Running a question's content words through corpus_search as built returns ZERO pages for 16 of 20 questions, including 13 of the 17 that ARE answerable. A 12-token question becomes a 12-way conjunction. Only the three shortest questions (2-3 content tokens: pl_14, pl_21, sd_03, sd_05) return anything at all. A floor built on this shape would declare "not in the corpus" for 13 of 17 questions whose evidence is sitting in the index. This is not a tuning detail; it is the reason the agent's own short phrases outperform the question text, and it was not previously recorded.

RESULT 2, NO SCORE FLOOR SEPARATES. Absence top1 under OR: -17.56, -28.61, -28.61. Evidence top1 under OR spans -10.59 to -54.40, so all three absence values sit INSIDE the evidence range. Overlap margin -18.0. Every candidate discriminator overlaps: OR top1 bm25 (-18.0), OR top1 per token (-1.99), OR matching pages (-913810), OR gap top1-to-top10 (-5.82), AND matching pages (0), identifier-AND pages (-5734). sd_03 is the clean illustration: a genuinely answerable question, 2 content tokens, 482 matching pages, top1 -20.27 - a WORSE score than two absence questions at -28.61. bm25 magnitude tracks query length and term rarity, not whether the answer exists, and in a 1.2M-page corpus an OR over common fiscal vocabulary matches 585k-914k pages no matter what is being asked.

RESULT 3, THE ONLY THING THAT LOOKS LIKE A SIGNAL, AND WHY IT IS NOT ADOPTABLE. All three absence questions name a SPECIFIC item rather than a topic: a fiscal year (2008-09) or a notification number (SRO 1500(I)/2024, SRO 1502(I)/2024). Probing identifiers taken from the question text only - never the key's absence_probe - the rarest identifier's page count is 5734 / 0 / 0 for the absent questions against a minimum of 487,610 for the evidence questions that have an identifier. That reads as a huge margin and it is reported as SEPARATES, but four things disqualify it as a floor. (a) It is scored on a SUBSET: 7 of 17 evidence questions contain no identifier at all, so the rule cannot fire on them - a rule that cannot fire is not a rule that works. (b) n=3 on the absence side. Three points cannot calibrate a threshold; they can only fail to rule one out. (c) FIXTURE-SPECIFIC, by this project's own claims-discipline rule: the token "sro" appears on ZERO of 1,206,260 indexed pages, so ab_11 and ab_13 are detected only because this harness happens to contain no SRO notifications whatsoever. Sir's real corpus is Pakistan fiscal and tariff material, where SROs certainly do appear, and the enabling condition is therefore ABSENT on the target. Barred from any headline or recommendation. (d) The one remaining case is contaminated: "2008" does appear on 5,734 pages, and the top hits are BIBLIOGRAPHY ENTRIES ("Qureshi, Ramsha Ali (2008). Agricultural Support Prices..."), not fiscal-year data. A count threshold over citation years is not a coverage test.

CONSEQUENCE. Do not pay for a cell to test a score floor - the offline evidence says it cannot work, for a structural reason rather than a tuning one: the score answers "is this topic in the corpus" and every question's topic is. Abstention needs a test of whether the SPECIFIC THING ASKED FOR is covered, which is a metadata question, not a ranking question - does any indexed document cover fiscal year X, does this notification number appear as an identifier anywhere. index_build.py already stores per-file status and page addresses, so a coverage dimension over periods and identifiers is buildable and testable offline, and unlike a floor it degrades honestly: it reports what it cannot check.
